title: Digital Ethiopia 2025: repeated failures to establish a national ID before Fayda
claim: Ethiopia's Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy documents that after multiple attempts at National ID projects over eight years (2010-2018) the Government had not been able to firmly establish a national ID, and that a digital ID program implementation had begun in Addis Ababa as a pilot.
evidence_summary: The Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy states that after multiple attempts of National ID projects over eight years from 2010 to 2018, the Government was not able to firmly establish a National ID, that the Ministry of Peace was setting the strategy for a National Digital ID, and that a Digital ID program implementation had begun in Addis Ababa potentially serving as a pilot.
source_excerpt: After multiple attempts of National ID projects over eight years from 2010 to 2018, the Government has not been able to firmly establish a National ID. Currently, the Ministry of Peace (MoP) is setting the strategy for a National Digital ID. A Digital ID program implementation has begun in Addis Ababa, which could potentially serve as a pilot for scaling up nationally subject to a review of its success.
interpretation: Policy evidence (government's own account) of the pre-Fayda institutional history: repeated implementation failure and pilot-stage rollout. This is a government self-assessment and therefore evidence of institutional capacity challenges, not an independent evaluation.
citation: Ministry of Innovation and Technology, 'Digital Ethiopia 2025: A Digital Strategy for Ethiopia Inclusive Prosperity', digital identity section.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the national digital strategy (digital identity chapter). Publication date not independently verified.
keywords: digital ID, Fayda, national ID, institutional capacity, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/5/digital-ethiopia-2025-strategy-english.pdf).

title: Digital Ethiopia 2025: cybersecurity assessment and capacity gaps acknowledged
claim: Ethiopia's Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy acknowledges that Ethiopia had not undergone a cybersecurity assessment to identify vulnerability, and faced a lack of cybersecurity experts and lack of user awareness.
evidence_summary: The Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy lists, as a key challenge for the cybersecurity sub-sector, that Ethiopia has not undergone a cybersecurity assessment to identify vulnerability, lacks cybersecurity experts and faces lack of awareness among users, and recommends a coordinated centralized assessment and national awareness campaigns.
source_excerpt: Key challenge for this sub-sector is Ethiopia has not undergone a cybersecurity assessment to identify vulnerability, lack of cybersecurity experts and lack of awareness among users. Recommendations to address critical gaps in cybersecurity are conducting a coordinated and centralized assessment of Ethiopia's cybersecurity, developing a framework and roadmap for national awareness campaigns.
interpretation: Policy evidence (government's own account) of cybersecurity institutional gaps. A government self-assessment; evidence of stated capacity gaps, not an independent measurement of security posture.
citation: Ministry of Innovation and Technology, 'Digital Ethiopia 2025', cybersecurity sub-sector section.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the national digital strategy (cybersecurity section). Publication date not independently verified.
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/5/digital-ethiopia-2025-strategy-english.pdf).
